headline: E-invoice mandate softened four times in nine months after Sabah loss
context: On 6 December 2025, a week after Pakatan Harapan's Sabah election loss, PM Anwar raised the e-invoice exemption from RM500K to RM1m. The RM1m-5m transition was extended on 5 January and 20 April 2026. From 1 September 2026 the exemption rose to RM3m.

changes.summary: Correction: Added the 20 April 2026 extension, making three softenings in five months, not two. Removed the ACCCIM estimate of 700,000 to 800,000 firms and the reported link to urban vote losses.

cards.big: On 6 December 2025, a week after Pakatan Harapan's Sabah election loss, PM Anwar raised the e-invoice exemption to RM1m turnover.
cards.sub: SAMENTA welcomed the move as relief for about 200,000 SMEs. The announcement came at a Sabah-Madani engagement days after the election.

cards.big: A 2023 government estimate put Malaysia's shadow economy near 21% of GDP, around RM330 billion. Other estimates run from 4% to 24.5%.
cards.sub: Khazanah Research Institute: informal sector 4.0-7.8% of GDP (2019). World Economics now shows 24.5%. Definitions and methods differ.

cards.big: By 22 December 2025 LHDN had logged 820.5 million e-invoices from 111,600 taxpayers: Phase 1-2 compliance over 90%, Phase 3 above 80%.
cards.sub: Volume more than doubled from 328m in June 2025. By 27 April 2026 LHDN said e-invoice checks had surfaced RM3.5 billion in undeclared income.

cards.big: The RM1m-5m transition was extended on 5 January 2026 (to end-2026) and 20 April (to end-2027). From 1 September 2026 the exemption threshold rose to RM3m.
cards.sub: LHDN's July 2025 checks had already flagged 5,800 taxpayers for RM484m undeclared prior-year income, about RM82m in additional tax.

cards.big: Phase 1-2 compliance is over 90%. Four softenings in nine months, first one week after a state election. The system scales when enforced; the rule moves on a political clock.
E-invoicing works where enforced: 820m invoices, over 90% Phase 1-2 compliance. Cost-relief has a stated rationale; four softenings in nine months set a different pattern.
